Moving the photo

Acts of Good · the Post it screen · 17 September 2026 · for your ruling

Photos now fill the frame, so nothing is white — and something always falls outside the edge. You asked to let people move the picture around rather than have the app choose. This is where that gets said. Every picture below is the real screen, not a drawing.

Where it is said

The drag itself is the same in all three. What changes is how somebody finds out it is there, which is the whole question — a drag nobody is told about is a drag nobody uses, which is the fault you flagged on the X.

If A, which wording

All three are one line in the same place. The first is yours, cleaned up.

One more, and I will decide it if you would rather not

Does the line stay for ever, or fade once they have moved a photo?

My answer: it stays. It costs one quiet line. Somebody posting their fortieth act in March has not thought about this since January, and a line that has removed itself is no help to them. A thing that teaches once and vanishes suits an app you use daily; this one you use weekly at most.

How to answer

A letter, and a number if you pick A — A1, B, C. Say fade if you want it to go away after the first move.

What is already built behind this

  • The photo fills the frame and starts in the middle. No white.
  • Where you move it to is kept, and survives closing the app.
  • On Instagram the photos are made to match the card so Instagram stops cropping them itself. On Facebook they are left alone.
  • The card is untouched on the feed — measured, not assumed.

The only thing missing is the way to say it, which is what this page is for.

Nothing on this page is built yet. Nothing has been pushed. Build in your hands is still 6O.
